data.title: A novel interaction site determines binding between AP180 and AP2 in clathrin mediated endocytosis
data.projectDescription: The early phases of clathrin mediated endocytosis are organized through a highly complex interaction network mediated by clathrin associated sorting proteins (CLASPs) that comprise long intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs). AP180 is a CLASP exclusively expressed in neurons and comprising a long IDR of around 600 residues, whose function remains partially elusive. Using NMR spectroscopy, we now describe a novel and strong interaction of AP180 with the major adaptor protein AP2 as well as its binding dynamics at atomic resolution. We find that the 70 residue long site determines the overall interaction between AP180 and AP2 in a dynamic equilibrium between its bound and unbound sate, while weaker binding sites contributing to the overall affinity at much high concentrations of AP2. Our data suggest that this novel interaction site might play a central role in recruitment of AP2 to the clathrin coated pit, whereas more transient and promiscuous interactions allow reshaping the interaction network until cargo uptake inside a coated vesicle.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Equal molar mixed AP180 and AP2β2 in 50 Mm Na-phosphate buffer was cross-linked with disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS, Cayman Chemical) using 1 mM final concentration for 15 minutes. The cross-linking reaction was quenched with 20 mM Tris-HCl (Carl Roth GmbH) for 15 min. For digestion, cross-linked proteins were denatured with 6 M Urea (Carl Roth), reduced with 10 mM dithiothreitol (DTT, VWR Life Science) at 37 °C for 45 min, and alkylated with 40 mM chloroacetamide (CAA, Sigma-Aldrich) at 37 °C for 45 min in the dark. After diluting to 2 M Urea with 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate buffer (TEAB, pH 8.0, Sigma-Aldrich), proteins were digested overnight with Glu-C (Promega) using an enzyme-to-protein ratio of 1:50 (w/w) at 37 °C. Peptides were desalted using StageTips filled with C8 material (CDS Analytical) and dried under SpeedVac.  Peptides were resuspended in 0.1% (v/v) Formic Acid (FA, biosolve Chimie SARL) for LC-MS/MS analysis. The analysis was performed on Vanquish Neo UHPLC system coupled with Orbitrap Exploris 480 (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Peptide separation was performed using a 50 cm reverse-phase column (in-house packed with Poroshell 120 EC-C18, 2.7 µm) with 180 min gradient. MS parameters were used as follows: MS1 resolution 120,000; MS2 resolution 30,000; charge state 4-8 enabled for MS2; higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) 30%; FAIMS CV -40/-50/-60 V.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data were searched against a fasta database comprised of AP180 and AP2β2 sequences using pLink 2.3.11. Searching parameters were set as follows: 10 ppm for MS1 spectra, 20 ppm for MS2 spectra. Searched result was separately filtered for intra-link and inter-link at 1% false discovery rate.
